subject.title: fix(mcp): honor `disabled` flag to prevent spawning disabled servers

question: Should OpenClaw permanently accept `disabled` as a public MCP configuration alias, or retain `enabled` as the sole runtime setting and support legacy files only through doctor migration?
rationale: This is a public configuration-contract decision with long-term upgrade and support consequences; the patch changes validation, config types, persisted writes, and runtime reads together.

options.title: Retain one canonical setting
options.body: Keep runtime and schema support to `enabled`, and repair legacy `disabled` files only through the doctor migration path.

options.title: Adopt `disabled` permanently
options.body: Accept and document `disabled` as a supported public alias, including precedence rules, upgrade behavior, and compatibility coverage.

recommendation.title: Retain one canonical setting
recommendation.body: Keep runtime and schema support to `enabled`, and repair legacy `disabled` files only through the doctor migration path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged MCP doctor work is the closest evidence-backed ownership signal for the migration boundary implicated by this decision.
